summary.tldr: Requires customs officers to detain some imports and creates a presumption that goods from certain countries or entities were made with forced or child labour.
what_it_does: Requires customs officers to detain certain goods until they are satisfied the goods are not prohibited imports under the Customs Tariff.
Creates a presumption that goods mined, manufactured, or produced in whole or in part in a designated country, area, or by a listed entity were made with forced labour or child labour.
Allows an importer to rebut that presumption by showing supply chain monitoring, supply management measures, prescribed certification or information, and due diligence.
Lets the Governor in Council designate countries or areas of concern, and establish a list of entities linked to forced labour or child labour.
Lets the Minister of Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness update or remove names on the entity list and requires a review of each listing every five years.
who_it_affects: Suppliers in designated countries or areas
summary.background: The bill amends the Customs Act and the Customs Tariff.
